name: BattleParty_ResetActiveRuntimeFields

score.note: Loops over each active party member (Func_080b6a60) and for each one zeros state+0x131..state+0x148 via a 3-byte countdown loop plus 22 individual byte stores, then calls Func_08077010. The reference's two interleaved even/odd store-pointer chains prove the zeroed range skips exactly one offset: 0x140 (not 0x142, an earlier hand-guess this session that measured byte-identically to 0x140's omission on raw counts alone -- the +2/+3 stride-jump position in the aligned disassembly is what actually distinguishes them, and 0x140 is the position that resolves every previously-marked instruction in the store-chain region). The u8 zero=0 local is hoisted to function scope (not per-iteration), matching the reference's r9-resident constant kept live across the whole loop.

remaining.where: prologue/loop register-allocation mismatch: candidate keeps the owners-pointer/count in r5/r9 with an extra movs/adds pair and issues the bge trip-check after loading the pointer, vs reference's r8/sl allocation with an early single-register move and cmp/bge issued before the mov sl step; plus an ldrsh-vs-ldrh signedness difference on the owners[i] load and a differing final pop/bx register pair. None of these are affected by the field-list choice -- raw differing_halfwords stays pinned near 109 across nearly all field-list variants because the extra prologue instructions phase-shift almost the entire body's byte offsets against the fixed-position reference comparison.
